title: Incident response for agents
point: Detect, contain, investigate, fix, then turn the incident into a regression case, so the same failure cannot ship twice.
definition: Incident response for agents is the practised sequence for handling harmful or anomalous behaviour in production. It covers detection, containment, investigation with traces, a fix, a regression case and a blameless review.

objective.text: Order the incident-response stages, name a concrete control for each, such as a kill switch, credential revocation or a golden-set regression case, and run a blameless review.

misconceptions.claim: The first job in an incident is to find the root cause.
misconceptions.correction: Contain first. Stop the harm with a kill switch, a lower rung of the degradation ladder or revoked credentials, then investigate from traces while nothing else leaks.

misconceptions.claim: Once the prompt is patched, the incident is closed.
misconceptions.correction: Without a regression case in the golden set, a later prompt or model change can bring the failure back unnoticed. Closing requires the test as well as the fix.

l1: Detect: guardrail metrics and alerts, such as a spike in blocked tool calls, outbound messages to new domains or refund volume above baseline.
Contain: a kill switch for the agent or one tool, a step down the degradation ladder to human handling, and revocation of any credentials that may be exposed.
Investigate with traces, fix the cause, and add the triggering input to the golden set as a regression case. Then hold a blameless post-incident review.
l2: An inbox agent's alert fires: replies to previously unseen domains jump from 3 to 40 in an hour. The on-call engineer disables the send tool, so the agent drops to drafts only.
Traces show one inbound email carrying hidden instructions to attach CRM exports. The engineer revokes the agent's CRM token and lists every affected message.
The fix quarantines inbound email and requires approval for attachments. The hostile email joins the golden set, and the review asks which control failed, not who failed.
l3: Track time to detect and time to contain separately. A kill switch that needs a deploy turns minutes of exposure into hours.
Practise containment. Run a regular exercise in which someone flips the kill switch and confirms the agent stops within the target time.
Feed the review into governance: update the risk register, the eval set and the incident records that frameworks or customers expect you to keep.
